appraisal_events.evidence: « saviez-vous qui est partisan enragé de Dreyfus ? […] Mon neveu Robert ! […] au Jockey, quand on a appris ces prouesses, cela a été une levée de boucliers, un véritable tollé. Comme on le présente dans huit jours… »
appraisal_events.explanation: The duc relays, as choice gossip, the Jockey Club's collective outcry against Saint-Loup's Dreyfusism, which threatens his imminent candidacy there; the sardonic "ces prouesses" and the deflating rejoinders that follow keep the passage from endorsing the club's verdict even as it registers the real social cost to Saint-Loup.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Évidemment […] s’ils sont tous comme Gilbert qui a toujours soutenu qu’il fallait renvoyer tous les Juifs à Jérusalem… » ; « Ah ! alors, le prince de Guermantes est tout à fait dans mes idées »
appraisal_events.explanation: The duchesse explains away the club's indignation by mockingly citing Gilbert's crude antisemitism, deflating the anti-Dreyfusard camp with a witty aside; d'Argencourt then takes her ridicule for endorsement and eagerly claims the same opinion, exposing himself in the process.

status_effects.explanation: His standing in the passage's aristocratic talk drops: he is the scandal of the moment, named as a "partisan enragé" whose conduct provoked a general outcry.
The outcry bears directly on his election at the Jockey in a week, putting his admission to that valued social space in doubt.
She interrupts and reframes the whole exchange with a single deflating witticism, controlling the tone of the conversation.
He is cited in absentia as the type of the crude bigot, his position quoted only to be laughed at.
By enthusiastically claiming the very opinion the duchesse has just mocked, he misses the irony and diminishes himself.

ambiguities: The stance toward the Jockey's condemnation of Saint-Loup could be read as flat neutral report of aristocratic gossip; it is taken here as ironized because the duc's "ces prouesses" is sardonic and because the duchesse's rejoinder and d'Argencourt's obtuse agreement immediately discredit the condemning voice within the same exchange.
The passage records the social cost of Saint-Loup's Dreyfusism without any local moral counter-praise, so no offsetting positive movement is assigned to him.
